orders.explanation: Transcript 1 methodically inspects the Django serializer, writes and applies a precise fix, updates both tests and documentation, and verifies everything with round-trip and full test suite checks. Transcript 2 stalls on test modifications and never achieves a clean pass.

Transcript 1 demonstrates a deep, systematic investigation—inspecting Django’s serializer code, reproducing the bug, crafting and applying a patch, updating tests and documentation, and running full test suites—whereas Transcript 2 only sketches the fix superficially. The thorough end-to-end workflow in Transcript 1 shows a higher level of expertise and capability.

Transcript 1 demonstrates deep understanding of the Django save machinery, reproduces the issue with a minimal script, inspects diffs, crafts and applies a targeted patch, and verifies it fixes the bug. Transcript 2 only locates code and stops without a complete diagnosis or fix.

Transcript 2 rapidly homes in on the existing regression fix in `_save_table`, correctly adds the `not raw` guard alongside the other conditions, and applies the minimal patch cleanly and succinctly. Transcript 1, by contrast, takes a much longer, more error-prone exploration and even generates a fix that breaks the existing test.

Transcript 1 methodically explores the codebase, identifies the precise change needed in alter_index_together (adding “unique: False” to the filter), updates both the implementation and related tests, and runs the full Django test suite to verify correctness across backends. Transcript 2 only demonstrates a quick repro and patch in isolation without integrating into migrations operations or the test suite.

Transcript 1 quickly hones in on the offending call to _delete_composed_index, patches it to pass {'index': True, 'unique': False}, and then validates the fix with minimal, focused repro steps. Transcript 2, by contrast, wanders through unrelated logs and test harness details at great length before arriving at essentially the same fix. The first is more direct and efficient, showing the hallmarks of a more capable model.

Transcript 2 patches only `query.py`, updates docs and some lookup tests, but leaves other test modules unverified and contains unresolved import errors.

Transcript 1 meticulously identifies the upstream commit fixing issue #10104, applies the exact minimal patch in `Catalog.__iter__`, adds a regression test and CHANGES entry, and thoroughly verifies with both unit and end-to-end tests. Transcript 2 attempts a custom deduplication but omits test and changelog updates and does not fully validate the fix.

Transcript 2 is from the more capable model because it discovers and applies the official upstream commit that fixes the issue, updates the CHANGES file and adds a proper regression test, and then fully verifies the fix with both the existing test suite and manual reproduction. Transcript 1, by contrast, implements a custom patch and runs manual checks but does not integrate the fix into the project’s changelog or test harness.

Transcript 1 shows deep code understanding, systematic use of repository exploration, precise patching of code, thorough testing (including edge cases), and documentation updates, indicative of a highly capable model. Transcript 2 barely begins exploration without implementing the feature.

Transcript 2 merely inspects code without delivering the full solution.

Transcript 2 is a convoluted, ad hoc set of scripts inserting a new parser helper without completing tests or changelog, showing far less polish and correctness.

Transcript 1, by contrast, wanders through ad hoc helper implementations and never settles on the concise patch.
